assigned.title: Playback-session candidate wire bounds match StreamCandidate bounds
assigned.acceptance: playbackSessionCandidateSchema uses THE SAME AUTHORITATIVE id and providerId limits as the StreamCandidate contract -- the exported MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_ID_CHARS and MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_PROVIDER_ID_CHARS -- and NOT copied numeric literals. PL-0708 exported those constants for exactly this reason; a copied literal would recreate the defect one layer out, which is the defect this task exists to close. Required: an oversized resolved candidate CANNOT RE-EXPAND ON THE SESSION WIRE after passing through another producer seam, which is the actual risk -- the contract bound governs what a provider may produce, and a second unbounded restatement downstream means the bound stops at the seam; fixture and Wikidata legitimate identifiers remain accepted, because a bound that rejects a real upstream id is an outage rather than a fix; tests cover the EXACT MAXIMUM, MAXIMUM PLUS ONE, and the serialized response, since a bound tested only from above does not prove the boundary is where it is claimed to be; reason and error output does not echo the oversized value; and NO SECOND INDEPENDENT BOUND VOCABULARY IS INTRODUCED. Note while working: playbackSessionCandidateSchema also carries unbounded uri and mimeType. They are not named in the reviewer's acceptance and are not in scope by default -- if they warrant bounds, say so and let the reviewer rule rather than adding them quietly.

typecheck.evidence: npx turbo run typecheck --force, exit 0, 21 of 21; lint --force, exit 0, 11 of 11; build --force, exit 0, 11 of 11. Three separate invocations. THE TYPECHECK GATE EARNED ITS PLACE THIS ROUND RATHER THAN RUBBER-STAMPING: it caught THREE defects in the new test file that vitest had already passed green, because vitest does not typecheck. A failoverPolicy literal carrying backoffMs and allowDowngrade, which that schema does not have (it has maxAttempts and maxTransientRetriesPerCandidate); a reason code 'candidates_authorized' that is not in the enum; and a reason object missing the required candidateId. Eleven tests were passing against all three. Recorded because the lead has cited this gate as routine in earlier rounds and it was not routine here. THE CHANGE: apps/web/src/app/api/v1/playback/session/contract.ts imports MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_ID_CHARS and MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_PROVIDER_ID_CHARS from @liberty/contracts/domains/playback -- a subpath the file already imported from -- and applies them to playbackSessionCandidateSchema's id and providerId. No new constant, no alias, no derived figure. docs/API_CONTRACTS.md states the bound, why the two seams are one value, and why uri and mimeType remain unbounded.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 20 of 20 tasks, 0 cached, 2734 passed 1 skipped against the 2723/1 baseline: +11, the whole of contract.bounds.test.ts; @liberty/web 908 to 919. Sum recomputed by the lead from the per-package figures: 100+67+68+47+208+252+373+260+288+152+919 = 2734. test:scripts 0 across six suites, repo:validate 0, ai:validate 0 at 66 tasks. THE BOUND IS TESTED AT THE BOUNDARY, NOT FROM ABOVE: exact maximum accepted and maximum-plus-one refused, for id and for providerId separately, because .max(200) also rejects a thousand characters and a test only from above locates nothing. Legitimate fixture and Wikidata-shaped identifiers are asserted still accepted, since a bound that rejects a real upstream id is an outage rather than a fix. TWO MUTANTS PLANTED AND BOTH KILLED, and the second is the one that matters. Removing .max(MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_ID_CHARS) fails 4 of 11. Replacing it with the COPIED LITERAL .max(141) -- runtime-identical, and exactly the defect this task exists to close -- fails 1 of 11, and it is the source-graph assertion that fires while every value test stays green. A numeric-equality suite alone would have permitted the defect, which is the same finding PL-0312 recorded about the health floor. THE RE-EXPANSION CLAUSE IS TESTED END TO END: an oversized candidate is refused by playbackSessionResponseSchema, which handler.ts validates every response against before it leaves, and a run through the real handlePlaybackSessionRequest with a resolver stub confirms the value does not reach a caller inside a granted session. THE FAILURE OUTPUT DOES NOT ECHO THE OVERSIZED VALUE: the serialized zod issues are asserted not to contain it, nor any forty-character run of it, while still carrying too_big and the candidates path. A FOURTH HARNESS DEFECT IS REPORTED HERE BECAUSE OF HOW IT HID: the handler test first passed an option named resolveAuthorizedCandidates -- the real option is resolve -- under an `as never` cast, so the stub was ignored, an ordinary session was produced, and the 200 read as a missing bound. The cast silenced the check that would have named it. The test now passes a correctly typed options object with no cast, and the comment in it says so. A test cast past the type system measures the cast.
